newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three French presumed killed in Comoros crash.
newsitem.headline: Three French presumed killed in Comoros crash.

text.p: Two of the five French nationals aboard the hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane which crashed off the Comoro Islands survived, but the three others were presumed dead, the foreign ministry said on Monday.

It said France had been deeply involved in rescue efforts, landing a medical aircraft and an air force Transall transport plane with a medical team from the Indian Ocean island of Reunion within five hours of Saturday's crash.
Both planes shuttled between Comoros and La Reunion, taking some 30 casualties to hospital in Reunion and returning with a 10-strong team of divers to help search for bodies.
The ministry did not identify the French casualties.

Of the 163 passengers and 12 crew on board the Boeing 767 that was hijacked en route to Nairobi and West Africa from Addis Ababa, 145 were international travellers from some 35 countries and thirty were Ethiopians.
Fifty-two people survived. The rest are dead or presumed dead. Police said on Monday that around 40 bodies had still to be recovered from the wreckage.
The French Defence Ministry said the two survivors were being flown home to France on a commercial flight scheduled to arrive in Paris early on Tuesday morning.
